concept.whyItMatters: Why does a 4,000-token RAG prompt answer in 150ms for the first word, yet take 8 seconds to finish streaming 400 words—and cost 4x more per output token? Because [LLM](/domains/llm) inference runs two completely different workloads: all input tokens fly through GPU tensor cores in parallel (Prefill), whereas every output token must stream model weights and the KV cache from HBM memory one token at a time (Decode). See how production gateways budget prompts and prefix caches in [Design an Enterprise RAG Gateway](/problems/design-enterprise-rag-gateway).
whenToUse: Budgeting context windows across system prompt, RAG chunks, chat history, and max_tokens output reserve.
Structuring prompts with static prefixes first to trigger provider KV/prompt caching.
whenNotToUse: Estimating token budgets by word count alone—code, JSON, and non-English text expand 2x–4x in token count.
keyPoints: Subword tokenization (BPE / SentencePiece): ~1 English token ≈ 4 chars (~0.75 words), whereas JSON punctuation, whitespace, and non-Latin scripts consume far more tokens per character.
Input tokens (Prompt): Processed in parallel in one Prefill pass—compute-bound (O(N²) attention), driving Time To First Token (TTFT).
Output tokens (Completion): Generated autoregressively one token at a time—HBM memory-bandwidth-bound, driving Time Per Output Token (TPOT) and total generation time.
Context window = Input tokens + Output tokens: both must fit inside `max_context_len`, and both allocate KV-cache memory for the duration of the request.

examples.title: RAG Prompt Budget & Cost Asymmetry
examples.scenario: A RAG assistant sends 6,000 input tokens (system prompt + 8 retrieved chunks) and generates 400 output tokens.
examples.outcome: Prefill processes all 6,000 input tokens in ~120ms (TTFT). Decode takes 400 sequential steps (~20ms/token = 8 seconds total). At $2.50/1M input and $10/1M output, the 400 output tokens cost ~$0.004 while the 6,000 input tokens cost ~$0.015—and caching the 2,000-token system prefix cuts input cost and TTFT further.

tradeOffs.con: Higher TTFT, larger KV cache, and 'lost-in-the-middle' dilution

tradeOffs.pro: Higher reasoning accuracy on hard tasks
tradeOffs.con: Linearly increases TPOT latency and 3x–5x output token cost

failureModes.name: Silent Output Truncation
failureModes.description: Input + output exceeds context window or hits `max_tokens`, cutting off JSON mid-object.
failureModes.mitigation: Reserve `max_tokens` upfront from the context budget and trim retrieved chunks/history before calling the model.

failureModes.name: Prompt Cache Busting
failureModes.description: Placing a dynamic timestamp or user ID at the start of the system prompt invalidates KV prefix caching on every request.
failureModes.mitigation: Put all static instructions and tool schemas first; append dynamic user/RAG context at the end.

commonMistakes: Assuming 1 word = 1 token across JSON, SQL, or multilingual text.
Placing dynamic variables at the top of the prompt, defeating KV prefix caching.

sections.content:
## Input vs. Output tokens at a glance

| Dimension | Input Tokens (Prefill) | Output Tokens (Decode) |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| Execution | Parallel across prompt | Sequential (1 token per step) |
| Hardware Bottleneck | GPU Tensor Core FLOPs | GPU HBM Memory Bandwidth |
| Latency Metric | TTFT (Time To First Token) | TPOT (Time Per Output Token) |
| Typical API Price | 1x baseline | 3x–5x higher per token |
| Caching | Prompt / KV prefix cacheable | Must be generated (unless speculative) |

## Reference implementation (Python — Context Window & Output Reserve Budgeter)

```python
# Deterministic context-window budgeter preventing output truncation (Python)
def fit_rag_chunks(system_tokens: int, query_tokens: int, chunks: list[tuple[str, int]],
                   max_context: int = 8192, reserve_output: int = 1024) -> list[str]:
    budget = max_context - reserve_output - system_tokens - query_tokens
    selected = []
    for text, tok_len in chunks:
        if tok_len <= budget:
            selected.append(text)
            budget -= tok_len
    return selected
```

pillars.label: Full Pipeline
pillars.summary: Text is tokenized via BPE, processed in parallel during Prefill to populate the KV cache, and then decoded one output token at a time.

pillars.label: Input (Prefill)
pillars.summary: Input tokens populate the KV cache in parallel. Static prefixes can be reused across requests via prompt caching.

pillars.label: Output (Decode)
pillars.summary: Each output token reads all model weights and the growing KV cache from HBM, making output tokens 3x–5x slower and pricier.

normal.heading: Step 1: Subword Tokenization
normal.desc: Prompt text is encoded into integer token IDs (~4 chars/token in English; denser in JSON/code).

normal.heading: Step 2: Parallel Prefill + Prefix Cache Hit
normal.desc: 1,500 static prefix tokens hit the KV prefix cache; GPU only computes Prefill for the 2,500 dynamic tokens.

fault.heading: Step 2 (CACHE MISS!): Timestamp at Top of Prompt
fault.desc: Placing `Current time: 14:15:02` on line 1 invalidates the entire 1,500-token prefix cache on every single call.

normal.heading: Step 3: Autoregressive Token Generation
normal.desc: Model emits 1 output token per step, appending its new K/V vectors to the KV cache until EOS or `max_tokens`.

options.label: 32K tokens (Full Docs)
options.note: Large input increases TTFT and KV-cache RAM per concurrent user.

failureMiniDiagrams.bottomBanner: FIX: STATIC PREFIX FIRST, DYNAMIC LAST

checklist: Always count tokens with the model's exact tokenizer—never assume 1 word == 1 token.
Reserve `max_tokens` for output before stuffing RAG chunks into the context window.
Keep static system prompts and tool definitions at the front of the prompt to hit KV prefix caches.

putItTogether.title: Put Input & Output Tokens together
putItTogether.summary: Put static system instructions first to hit KV prefix caches, reserve `max_tokens` before stuffing RAG chunks, and keep outputs concise.
steps: Count tokens with the target tokenizer and reserve output `max_tokens` first.
Put static instructions/tools first for KV prefix caching; place dynamic RAG/user text last.
Track TTFT (Prefill) and TPOT (Decode) separately in production telemetry.
putItTogether.outcome: Predictable latency, zero JSON truncation, and 50%+ lower inference spend.

tipsAndTricks: Output tokens dominate both end-to-end streaming latency (TPOT) and API cost (3x–5x input token pricing).
A single dynamic character at byte 0 of a system prompt invalidates the entire prefix KV cache.
